heroStatement:
Personal care
before and after surgery
approachLead: In a specialty that deals with sensitive concerns, care goes beyond a diagnosis. Each person needs to understand what is happening and feel able to ask any question.
approachText: During a consultation, I listen, explain the examination and discuss treatment options. If surgery is needed, I explain the procedure and recovery in advance.
approachCore: My work does not end with the operation. I personally care for my surgical patients before and after their procedure.
step1Text: Understand your concerns and what matters to you.
step2Text: Discuss diagnostic tests and possible treatment options.
step3Text: Choose a treatment plan based on the diagnosis, clinical indications and your health.
step4Text: Provide follow-up care after surgery and discuss your recovery.

clinicalText1: My experience spans city hospitals and private clinics, colorectal surgery, general surgery and the surgical treatment of infections.
clinicalText2: I use non-surgical, minimally invasive and surgical treatments. The approach depends on each person's diagnosis and health.
method1Text: Non-surgical treatment, sclerotherapy, rubber band ligation, infrared coagulation, hemorrhoidal dearterialization, laser vaporization and hemorrhoidectomy. The method is chosen after assessment, according to clinical indications.
method2Text: Assessment and treatment planning. Excision of anal fissures and fistulas, with sphincteroplasty when indicated. Follow-up care during recovery.
method3Text: Assessment, discussion of treatment options, pilonidal cyst excision and postoperative care.
method4Text: Removal of external hemorrhoids, anal skin tags, papillomas and condylomas. Abscess incision and drainage when indicated.
method5Text: Examination, anoscopy and proctoscopy when indicated. I explain why a test is needed, what the results show and which next steps I recommend.
recoveryLead: I apply fast-track surgery principles in my surgical practice.
recoveryText1: This approach coordinates treatment and recovery. When the clinical indications and the patient's health allow, surgery may be followed by discharge home on the same day. The decision is always made individually.
recoveryText2: Before surgery, we discuss preparation and follow-up care. Afterwards, I continue to care for the patient throughout recovery.
archiveText: Back in 2019, Angelina discussed the use of fast-track principles in colorectal surgery. Promotional material from the clinic.
quote1: “She examined me very gently, explained every step and reassured me.”
quote2: “She listens and explains everything in plain language anyone can understand.”
timeline2Text: Postgraduate internship in surgery at Izhevsk State Medical Academy. Specialist retraining in colorectal surgery at Nizhny Novgorod State Medical Academy.
timeline3Text: Practice at City Clinical Hospitals No. 2 and No. 6. Also worked as a surgeon in the surgical infections department at City Clinical Hospital No. 6 in 2020–2021.
timeline5Text: With MEDSI since November 2024. I currently see patients at MEDSI Premium on Krasnaya Presnya.

prepTitle: How to prepare for a coloproctology appointment
prepNoTitle: When bowel preparation is NOT needed
prepNoLead: Do not use enemas to prepare:
prepNo2: if you have severe pain around the anus;
prepNoAfter: In these situations, come to your appointment without bowel preparation.
prepImportant: If you are unsure whether preparation is needed in your situation, it is better to come without it. The doctor will decide during the appointment which examinations are appropriate and how much examination is needed.
prepFoodText: Do not eat during the two hours before your appointment. You may drink water.
prepMorningTitle: If your appointment is in the morning
prepMorningText: If you have had a spontaneous bowel movement that morning, additional preparation with a micro-enema is not needed.
prepAfternoonTitle: If your appointment is in the afternoon
prepAfternoonText: Use Microlax or Enema Klin 2–3 hours before your appointment.
prepBring2: Previous consultation notes, discharge summaries and examination results, if available.
prepBring3: A list of medicines you take regularly.
prepMissingDocs: Not having previous medical records or examination results does not prevent you from having a consultation.
visitTitle: What happens at your first coloproctology appointment
visitPause: You can ask to pause or stop the examination.
visitTalkText1: The appointment begins with a conversation. The doctor will ask what is troubling you, when your symptoms started and which treatments you have already tried.
visitTalkText2: You may be asked about bowel movements, pain, bleeding or discharge, previous illnesses and operations, and the medicines you take. Explain what worries you most and which questions you would like to discuss.
visitExamText1: The doctor first examines the area around the anus. If needed, this is followed by a digital rectal examination and anoscopy: an examination of the anal canal using a small specialised instrument.
visitExamText2: The extent of the examination is decided individually, taking your symptoms and how you feel into account. Not every appointment requires all of these examinations.
visitExamText3: Before each procedure, the doctor will explain what they intend to do and why it is needed.
visitPainTitle: If you feel afraid or have pain
visitPainText1: Tell the doctor before the examination begins. During the examination, also report any pain or discomfort.
visitPainText2: If pain is severe, the doctor may adjust the examination, use local anaesthesia or postpone part of it.
visitPlanTitle: After the examination: an explanation and a plan
visitPlanText1: The doctor will explain the findings and the diagnosis or preliminary assessment. If further examinations are needed, their purpose will be explained.
visitPlanText2: You will then discuss treatment options, their benefits, limitations and expected results. The approach is chosen with regard to medical indications and your preferences.
visitImportant1: You can ask questions and request another explanation of anything that remains unclear.
visitImportant2: The purpose of the first appointment is to understand your situation and make a plan for the next steps. The extent of the examination should be justified and take your condition into account.
